name: Siwa Town and Shali
tagline: Around the dissolving mudbrick fortress in the centre
description: The centre of the oasis, built around Shali, the mudbrick citadel that a rare three-day rain largely dissolved in 1926 and which still stands over the town as an eroded mass. The market, the few restaurants, the bike rentals and the guides are all in the square below it.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the market, the guides and the fortress within a short walk
pros: Shali, the market and the town square all together
Bicycle rental for the whole oasis
The only connectivity and services in Siwa
cons: Donkey carts and traffic through the square
Conservative, so dress and behaviour matter

name: Aghurmi and the Oracle
tagline: The old village on the rock where Alexander came
description: A settlement a few kilometres east built on and around the rock holding the Temple of the Oracle, where Alexander the Great came in 331 BC to be confirmed as a son of Amun. Palm gardens, springs and the remains of the older village surround it.
bestFor: Stays that want the oracle temple and the palm gardens on the doorstep
pros: The Temple of the Oracle and Cleopatra's spring nearby
Dense palm gardens and irrigation channels
Quiet and green by oasis standards
cons: A bicycle or vehicle is needed for the town

name: Fatnas and the Salt Lakes
tagline: The island in the salt lake, west of town
description: A palm-covered spit reaching into Birket Siwa, the salt lake west of the town, known for the sunset and for the water dense enough to float in. The salt pans nearby are brilliant white and blue, and there are a handful of ecolodges along the shore.
bestFor: Stays that want the salt lakes and the sunsets rather than the town
pros: The salt lakes, the pans and the floating pools
The best sunsets in the oasis
Ecolodges built in the local salt and mudbrick technique
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes from town by bicycle
No shops or services at all
Mosquitoes near the water at dusk

name: Dakrour and the Southern Gardens
tagline: Below the mountain, where the sand baths are
description: The area south of the town around Gebel Dakrour, a hill known for a traditional sand-burial treatment for joint pain that people still travel for in summer, surrounded by olive and date gardens. Quiet, rural and a short ride from the centre.
bestFor: Quiet stays among the date and olive gardens
pros: Olive and date gardens and the springs among them
A short bicycle ride from town

name: Great Sand Sea Edge
tagline: Where the palms stop and the dunes begin
description: The southwestern edge of the oasis where the cultivation ends abruptly and the Great Sand Sea runs unbroken for hundreds of kilometres. A few desert camps operate out here. Travel beyond the edge requires military permission arranged through a licensed operator.
bestFor: Short stays in a desert camp rather than a base of any kind
pros: The dunes and the night sky, both exceptional
Desert camps and dune trips from the edge
cons: Permits and a licensed operator are required to go beyond
